sfmun-xii-2027.about:
SFMUN is San Francisco's annual one-day Model UN conference, held at Lowell High School and now in its 12th session.

The conference runs 23 January 2027 at Lowell High School, San Francisco, United States. It is open to middle and high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Registration opened 1 Nov 2026; regular registration closes 29 Nov 2026 and late registration runs 30 Nov – 29 Dec 2026. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 23 January 2027 in San Francisco, United States
One-day conference — good first MUN
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
sfmun-xii-2027.eligibility: Open to middle and high school students and school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Registration opened 1 Nov 2026; regular registration closes 29 Nov 2026 and late registration runs 30 Nov – 29 Dec 2026.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
sfmun-xii-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

The conference runs 16–18 April 2027 at UC San Diego, La Jolla, United States. It is open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

sharkbyte-2026.about:
SharkByte 2026 is Miami Dade College's signature weekend-long tech hackathon. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at Miami Dade College in Miami from 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-08. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Free entry, food and mentoring
Official MLH 2027 season event
Build a portfolio project in one weekend
sharkbyte-2026.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.

Attend in person and submit your project for judging
sharkbyte-2026.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

sheridan-datathon-2026.about:
Sheridan Datathon 2026 is a student-led 24-hour data-science hackathon at Sheridan College. It takes place in person in Mississauga from 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08, organised by Sheridan College.

Participants team up, attend workshops, build a working project and present it to judges. Food and workspace are provided free; travel is usually self-funded unless the organisers announce support.

MLH member event

shpgmun-2027.about:
SHPGMUN is the Model United Nations conference of Stonyhurst International School Penang. It runs on 5–7 March 2027 on the school campus in Penang, Malaysia, with committees using a modified Harvard rules of procedure, a delegate handbook, position-paper and draft-resolution guides and a social night on 6 March.

Individual delegates and groups (6+ delegates) from other schools can register; chaperones and observers aged 16+ register separately.

A friendly, well-documented school conference for students in Malaysia and the region.
highlights: Delegate handbook and writing guides for beginners
Individual and group registration
Social night on 6 March
shpgmun-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students (individuals or school groups). English is the working language.

Meet the 8 Jan 2027 regular deadline (late until 7 Feb)
Prepare with the handbook and attend 5–7 March
shpgmun-2027.costs: Delegate fees listed in the registration form; groups pay a lump sum. Travel and accommodation extra.

simun-2027.about:
SIMUN is a three-day spring conference for high-school students run by GLICA, the organiser of GLIMUN, held in Lansing, Michigan. First-time delegates are welcome.

The conference runs 25–27 February 2027 at AC Hotel & Hyatt House Lansing, Michigan, United States. It is open to high school students; first-time delegates welcome. Working language: English.

Schools register on glica.org; early deadline 11 Dec 2026, regular deadline 11 Jan 2027; delegate drop deadline 25 Jan; position papers due 19 Feb 2027. Delegate, advisor and hotel rates are posted on the SIMUN 'Costs and Hotel' page (published by Nov 2026). As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

simun-xxii-2027.about:
SIMUN (Singapore International Model United Nations) is held annually for three days in March at the International French School (IFS) in Singapore and is affiliated with the THIMUN Foundation. Committees typically include DISEC, ECOSOC, HRC, the Security Council, SPECPOL, WHO and a historical security council.

School participation is by invitation; MUN directors who want to attend should contact the IFS organisers to express interest. SIMUN XXII is listed for 18–20 March 2027.

A classic THIMUN-style school conference in Singapore with a strong regional following.
highlights: THIMUN-affiliated
Hosted by the International French School
Classic THIMUN committee set
simun-xxii-2027.eligibility: High-school students attending with an invited school delegation. English is the working language.

Attend 18–20 March 2027

snu-international-summer-program-2027.about:
Since 2007 more than two thousand students have joined the SNU International Summer Program (ISP), an intensive summer session at Korea's most prestigious university. Courses are taught in English by SNU and visiting faculty, covering Korea and East Asia (including Hallyu, K-pop and K-drama) as well as business, social sciences, sciences and more; students can take up to 9 credits, live in the campus dormitory and join field trips and cultural activities around Seoul.

Registration usually opens in early January, with a 20% tuition discount for registering by early April. The programme suits university students who want transferable credits and an immersive summer in Korea; high-school graduates already admitted to a university can also apply.
highlights: Up to 9 SNU credits in English-taught courses
Korean studies plus a wide range of other subjects
20% early-bird tuition discount; campus dormitory and field trips
snu-international-summer-program-2027.eligibility: University students from any country, and high-school graduates admitted to a university for the autumn semester. All nationalities.
how_to_apply: Join the ISP mailing list or check summer.snu.ac.kr from January 2027
Register and choose courses online (early-bird by about 5 April)
Submit enrolment/admission proof and passport details
Pay the invoice (application fee, tuition, optional dorm and field trip) by mid-May
snu-international-summer-program-2027.costs: 2026: application fee KRW 200,000; tuition KRW 1,800,000 for one 3-credit course up to KRW 3,348,000 for up to 9 credits (20% early-bird discount); dormitory KRW 1,100,000; field trip KRW 300,000. Meals extra.

snu-international-winter-program-2026-27.about:
Seoul National University's International Winter Program runs from 19 December 2026 to 9 January 2027 on the Gwanak campus. Students take English-taught courses for 3 or 5 SNU credits (classes 21 December – 8 January, with final exams on the last day), live in the SNU dormitory and join curated field trips (26 December and 2 January) to regional cities, local festivals and lesser-known attractions, plus winter sports and K-pop dance classes.

The programme is open to university students and to high-school graduates admitted to a university for spring 2027. The deadline is very close, so apply immediately if interested.
highlights: 3 or 5 SNU credits in three weeks
Field trips, winter sports and Korean culture activities
Korea's most prestigious university
snu-international-winter-program-2026-27.eligibility: Current university students worldwide, and high-school graduates admitted to a university for spring 2027. Open to all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Read the 2026–27 IWP announcement and leaflet on summer.snu.ac.kr
Apply and register for courses by 6 November 2026
Pay fees (application, tuition, dormitory) by 13 November 2026
Apply for a Korean visa if required
snu-international-winter-program-2026-27.costs: Tuition KRW 1,800,000 (3 credits, about USD 1,330) or KRW 2,790,000 (5 credits, about USD 2,060); application fee KRW 200,000; dormitory KRW 660,000 for 3 weeks. Meals and flights extra.

south-summit-brazil-startup-competition-.about:
South Summit Brazil is the Latin American edition of the South Summit innovation event, held in Porto Alegre on 14-16 April 2027. The 2026 competition drew startups from more than 66 countries.

After registration, a jury reviews applications in January and selects 50 finalists, announced in February. Finalists pitch on stage for three minutes to international investors, funds and corporates, compete for five prizes and get networking and deal-making opportunities.

Registration closes on 14 December 2026 on the South Summit Brazil page.
highlights: 50 finalists pitch to international investors
Startups from 66+ countries in 2026
Free registration
south-summit-brazil-startup-competition-.eligibility: Startups from any country with an innovative, scalable solution.
how_to_apply: Open the South Summit Brazil startup competition page.
Complete your registration and startup profile.
Submit by 14 December 2026.
If selected (February), pitch in Porto Alegre on 14-16 April 2027.
south-summit-brazil-startup-competition-.costs: Free to apply; travel and accommodation are the startup's own.

south-summit-madrid-startup-competition-.about:
South Summit is one of Europe's leading innovation events, held every June in Madrid. Its Startup Competition is open to startups from any country; you do not need to be incorporated or have a finished product, only an innovative project with a team.

Around 400 startups are preselected around February, and the final 100 finalists pitch on stage in Madrid in front of investors, corporations and media, with category winners and an overall winner. Finalists get free passes, matchmaking with investors and visibility.

Complete your profile on the application platform in English; you can edit a draft until the deadline of 31 January 2027.
highlights: Free to apply, open worldwide
100 finalists pitch at South Summit Madrid
Investor matchmaking and visibility
south-summit-madrid-startup-competition-.eligibility: Startups and early projects from any country; no incorporation or product required. Application in English.

Complete your startup profile in English.
Submit by 31 January 2027.
If preselected, take part in jury rounds; finalists pitch in Madrid in June.
south-summit-madrid-startup-competition-.costs: Free to apply; finalists receive event passes. Travel is at your own cost.

stanford-aimi-summer-research-internship.about:
The AIMI Summer Research Internship gives high-school students mentored, hands-on research experience at the intersection of AI and medicine (medical imaging, clinical data, health equity), with lectures from Stanford researchers and a final project presentation.

The 2027 application opens on 10 November 2026 with a free online information session that day (5–6 pm PT) and closes on 1 February 2027. The page does not state nationality limits or fees, so ask at the info session or email aimi-hs-programs@stanford.edu.

stanford-sumac-2027.about:
SUMaC introduces strong high-school students to university-level abstract mathematics through lectures, problem sessions and a research-style group project, taught by Stanford-affiliated instructors. In 2026 it offered a 4-week residential session on the Stanford campus (21 June – 17 July, 40 places) and two 3-week online sessions (64 places each) with live classes.

It is open to students from around the world currently in grades 10–11. Fees are high (2026: USD 8,950 residential, USD 3,750 online), but Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies offers need-based financial aid to domestic and international applicants, and applying for aid does not affect admission.
highlights: University-level abstract algebra, number theory or topology with group research projects
Residential on Stanford campus or live online
Need-based aid available to international students
stanford-sumac-2027.eligibility: Students in grades 10–11 (rising juniors and seniors) from any country with strong maths preparation and good English.

Request financial aid in the application if needed and submit documents via SSS by the aid deadline (early February in 2026)
Decisions follow in spring
stanford-sumac-2027.costs: 2026: USD 8,950 residential (housing, meals, supplies, trips) or USD 3,750 online. Financial aid application fee USD 60 (waivers available). Need-based aid for domestic and international students.

student-academy-awards-2027.about:
The Student Academy Awards, run by the organisation behind the Oscars, have launched the careers of many acclaimed directors. Entrants must be post-secondary students in a degree or certificate programme whose film (up to 40 minutes) was made as part of coursework.

Winning films become eligible for Oscar consideration in the short film categories, and winners are honoured at an awards ceremony (2026's was held at TIFF Lightbox, Toronto). One film per director per year; entry is free.
highlights: Free, open to film students worldwide
Four categories incl. animation and documentary
Winners eligible for Oscar shorts consideration
student-academy-awards-2027.eligibility: Directors who are post-secondary students in a degree or certificate programme when the film was made; film made as coursework, max 40 minutes, completed within the eligibility window; one entry per director.
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 rules when published on oscars.org/saa

Submit online during the spring window

summer-at-brown-2027.about:
Summer@Brown is Brown University's main summer programme for high-school students: short, seminar-style courses (no grades or credit) across the sciences, humanities, social sciences, arts and leadership, taught by Brown faculty and experts. Students live in Brown residence halls in Providence, commute, or study online.

In 2026 on-campus courses ran 21 June – 24 July; residential prices ranged from USD 3,748 (1 week) to USD 8,372 (3 weeks), and online courses from USD 3,364. International students are common (75+ countries) and pay an extra USD 80 accident-insurance fee. Brown offers some need-based scholarships.
highlights: Wide choice of 1–6 week courses taught by Brown instructors
Residential, commuter or online
Students from 75+ countries
summer-at-brown-2027.eligibility: High-school students (typically grades 9–12) from any country; English proficiency is considered for course enrolment.
how_to_apply: Browse 2027 courses when published
Start the online application (opened mid-January in 2026)
Submit statement, transcript and English proficiency evidence if required
Apply for need-based scholarships early
Enrol and pay once admitted

summer-at-epfl-2027.about:
Summer@EPFL invites strong bachelor's and master's students from around the world to spend two to three months (usually between May and September, dates agreed with the host lab) doing research in one of the labs of EPFL's School of Computer and Communication Sciences in Lausanne: machine learning, systems, security, theory, networking, signal processing and more.

Fellows receive CHF 1,800 per month (prorated) plus a refund of travel costs (economy flight or second-class train). Selection is highly competitive and based on academic results; many fellows go on to PhD programmes at EPFL and other top universities.
highlights: Research internship in a top-ranked computer science school
CHF 1,800/month stipend plus travel refund
Strong pathway to EPFL master's and PhD programmes
summer-at-epfl-2027.eligibility: Bachelor's (at least 2nd year) or master's students, or equivalent, in computer science, computer engineering, telecommunications or electrical engineering. PhD students are not eligible. Open worldwide.

summit-mun-2026.about:
Summit MUN is a four-day Model United Nations conference held at the five-star Berjaya Times Square Hotel in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on 14–17 December 2026. It follows official UN-style rules of procedure, with a team of coaches supporting every committee and workshops for first-time delegates.

swedish-institute-si-academy-eastern-eur.about:
SI Academy: Eastern Europe brings together six thematic training programmes delivered by Swedish universities and organisations with local partners: Transparency Practices in Open and Digital Collaborative Policy-Making (Halmstad University), STRIDE on digital democracy (Linköping and Tartu universities), Democratic European Accession Negotiations (Stockholm Institute of Transition Economics), cultural policy, participatory governance (PARTGOV, Malmö University) and democratic leadership through popular education (ABF Hälsingland). It replaces the former Swedish Institute Academy for Young Professionals (SAYP).

Applicants must be citizens or residents of Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova or Ukraine, have good English, a degree of at least three years, and current employment relevant to the programme. In Belarus and Georgia, participation is currently limited to representatives of civil society organisations, and not every programme is open to every country.

Applications go directly to each programme organiser; calls open between October and December and close by January 2027. You may apply to a maximum of two programmes. Participants join the Sweden Alumni Network.

Georgia eligible (civil-society representatives)
Membership of the Sweden Alumni Network

Georgia and Belarus: civil-society representatives only. Programme-specific rules apply.

tartu-mudel-uro-2027.about:
Tartu Mudel ÜRO is the UN simulation run by the United Nations Association of Estonia under the EU co-funded NextGen UN project. It brings upper-secondary and university students to Tartu for five UN committees (including the Security Council and Human Rights Council), a press team and one English-language committee, plus expert meetings and an evening programme.

The conference runs 5–7 February 2027 at venues in Tartu, Estonia. It is open to young people aged 15–23 (upper-secondary and university students). Working language: Estonian (plus one English-language committee).

Registration opens on the official site (a countdown is shown); choose a committee/topic when you register. Participation fee: €20 or €25 (official site). tca-connected-with-the-world-amersfoort-.about:
This Dutch-language TCA (1–4 February 2027, Amersfoort) is organised by the Netherlands National Agency (Nuffic) around its conference "Samen leren, klaar voor de wereld". It explores how multilingualism, (global) citizenship, internationalisation and resilience come together in daily teaching, and how Erasmus+ and eTwinning can support cooperation on these themes.

It targets schools in regions outside the Randstad (border regions, Wadden Islands, the Caribbean Netherlands), German schools where Dutch is taught, and Flemish schools. Day 2 is a full TCA programme, day 3 the Nuffic conference, day 4 a reflection session.

70 places: about 50 for the Netherlands and 15–17 for Germany; Flemish teachers can express interest by email (tca@erasmusplus.nl).

tca-demystifying-vet-mobility-dublin-202.about:
Demystifying Erasmus+ VET Mobility Projects is a Training and Cooperation Activity hosted by Léargas, the Irish National Agency, in Dublin (24–27 January 2027). It is for newcomers and less experienced organisations in vocational education and training (VET) that want to run or apply for Key Action 1 mobility.

Sessions cover KA1 VET rules and compliance, the Erasmus Quality Standards, pre-departure preparation and risk protocols for learners, tracking learning outcomes and impact, and dissemination. Participants draft project ideas with potential partners for upcoming rounds.

Forty places for VET coordinators, international officers, school directors and mobility managers from about 17 countries.

tca-euroapprentices-regional-meeting-olo.about:
EuroApprentices are vocational students and apprentices who completed an Erasmus+ placement abroad and now promote VET mobility. Their 2026 regional meeting, a Training and Cooperation Activity of the Czech National Agency (DZS), takes place in Olomouc on 4–6 December 2026.

About 40 EuroApprentices (10 per country) plus NA staff from Austria, Czechia, Poland and Slovakia will exchange experiences, build ties through interactive workshops, networking sessions and cultural activities, and plan how to promote the EuroApprentices initiative.

It is one of the few TCAs aimed at learners rather than staff. The deadline is very close: 1 November 2026.

tca-green-skills-first-steps-istanbul-20.about:
First Steps in Erasmus+: Green Skills for School Education is a TCA organised by the Turkish National Agency in Istanbul (7–10 December 2026), part of the long-term activity 'Sustainability and Greening+'. It supports the Erasmus+ priority 'Environment and the fight against climate change'.

Through workshops, collaborative activities and peer learning, primary and secondary school teachers explore how GreenComp, the European sustainability competence framework, translates into teaching and school practice, develop their own sustainability competences and exchange good practice. They also build partnerships for future KA1 and KA2 projects with a green focus.

About 70 participants, from Türkiye and around 13 other Erasmus+ countries.

tca-mobility-consortia-quality-cologne-2.about:
This TCA (23–25 May 2027, Cologne) is the eighth conference organised by the German National Agency for school education (PAD) for coordinators of accredited Erasmus+ mobility consortia, preferably those run by school authorities or coordination bodies. With the UK and possibly Switzerland returning to Erasmus+ in 2027, potential coordinators from those countries can also meet European counterparts.

The programme focuses on sharing proven models, partner reliability, inclusion and accessibility, and planning high-quality mobility. Changes in the next programme generation will be discussed, and the European Association of Training Providers (EATP) will attend to discuss course quality.

About 170 places are available, at least three per country.

The Online Partner Finding Fair is a Training and Cooperation Activity (TCA) run online by DZS, the Czech National Agency for Erasmus+, on 11 November 2026 (15:00–16:30 CET). It is for lower- and upper-secondary teachers (learners aged 13–18) who take part in Erasmus+ KA1 school projects (KA122 short-term or KA120 accredited).

After a short introduction, participants meet potential partners in breakout rooms ('speed dating'), present their projects and exchange contacts, aiming to find hosting schools for pupil or staff mobility, job-shadowing partners or schools for online cooperation.

About 60 places are shared among Czech participants and colleagues from Slovenia, Latvia, Denmark, Cyprus, Croatia, Luxembourg, Austria, Greece, Finland, Türkiye, Poland, Malta, Germany, Portugal and Sweden.

tca-project-idea-to-application-liechten.about:
This contact seminar (18–21 January 2027, Hotel kommod, Ruggell) is organised by AIBA, Liechtenstein's National Agency, for organisations from German-speaking regions in all sectors: school, VET, adult, higher education and youth. The working language is German.

Participants bring their own project idea or join a group, and work through needs analysis, SMART objectives, project structure and RACER indicators, budgeting, impact and dissemination, and how AI can be used acceptably in application writing, ending with all elements needed for a KA220 Cooperation Partnership application. A city tour and visit to the Liechtenstein National Museum in Vaduz are included.

About 78 places, mostly for Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany and German-speaking Belgium, with a few for Italy, Czechia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Luxembourg and Denmark.

tca-schools-in-transition-conference-boc.about:
This European conference (19–21 April 2027, Bochum) is a transnational TCA hosted by PAD, the German National Agency for Erasmus+ school education, with the Spanish and Finnish agencies. The Ruhr region's history of industrial change and migration is the backdrop for discussing how schools respond to geopolitical, social and economic transformation.

The format is a BarCamp: participants propose and lead sessions on how Erasmus+ and eTwinning can support inclusion, social cohesion, democratic participation and the well-being and resilience of pupils and teachers. An optional session shows how to start an eTwinning project.

About 150 headteachers, teachers and support staff who are current Erasmus+ beneficiaries will attend. Priority goes to schools with diverse pupils, in disadvantaged or rural areas. Good English is essential.

Zorg voor Taal (14–16 April 2027, Hotel The Den, 's-Hertogenbosch) is a TCA of the Netherlands National Agency for teachers and coordinators in vocational (mbo) care and health programmes from the Netherlands and Flanders, working with students aged about 16+.

The seminar covers language competences and (digital) literacy of care students, the use of AI, Dutch and Flemish good practices, and analysis of participants' own institutions' language challenges. A study visit to an mbo institution is included.

tech-for-community-hackathon-2026.about:
Tech For Community Hackathon 2026 is a high-school hackathon where teams build technology for local community problems. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at TecNurtur in St. John's from 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-22. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.

tech-for-community-hackathon-2026.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

the-odin-project-full-stack.about:
The Odin Project is a free, open-source curriculum for learning web development from scratch. It guides you through foundations (HTML, CSS, Git, command line) and then a full-stack path in either JavaScript (Node.js/React) or Ruby on Rails, with many portfolio projects.

It is maintained by volunteers and supported by an active Discord community where learners get help and code reviews. There are no deadlines, fees or applications; you progress at your own pace.

It is ideal for students who want a structured, project-based path to junior developer skills without paying for a bootcamp.

Project-based full-stack curriculum
Large, helpful learner community

timisoara-mun-2026.about:
Timișoara International MUN ('Bridging Ideas, Shaping Futures') brings delegates to western Romania for committees such as UNICEF. Its website is the conference's official registration platform.

The conference runs 27–29 November 2026 at venues in Timișoara, Romania. It is open to high school and university students. Working language: English.

Create an account on the official site (email or Google), choose committee and country preferences and submit the application. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Tobitate! (Leap for Tomorrow) is a public-private study-abroad initiative of Japan's Ministry of Education (MEXT) run with JASSO and corporate donors. In the 'New Japan Representative Programme' 12th cohort for high-school students, 600 students (STEAM 140, sports/arts 120, 'my curiosity' 210, social issues 130) design their own stay abroad of 14 days to one year, starting between 10 July 2027 and 31 March 2028.

Support: monthly scholarship of 120,000 or 160,000 yen depending on destination (60,000 yen above the income threshold) and a preparation grant of 150,000 yen (Asia) or 250,000 yen (elsewhere). First-round applications run from early December 2026 to 21 January 2027; a second round (100 places) runs 1-21 April 2027.

tobitate-university-19th-2027.about:

tokyo-marathon-2027-global-volunteers.about:
The Tokyo Marathon is one of the six Abbott World Marathon Majors. For the 2027 race (Sunday 7 March 2027) the Tokyo Marathon Foundation recruits "Global Volunteers" from overseas through VOLUNTAINER, its official volunteer club, as part of a team of about 10,000 volunteers.

Global Volunteers hand out water, sports drinks, snacks and sponges at aid stations along the course (blocks from Suidobashi and Kanda to Ginza, Asakusa and Shiba) or distribute items to runners at the finish near Tokyo Station, usually between about 8:00 and 18:00. Before the race each volunteer must attend in-person check-in and the mandatory information session at Tokyo Big Sight (4, 5 or 6 March 2027). Assignments are announced in mid-January 2027.

Volunteers receive official volunteer wear and a cap, and a certificate of activity on request. It is a short, low-commitment way to be part of a world-class sporting event and meet volunteers from many countries.

Free to join; official volunteer wear and activity certificate

tony-elumelu-foundation-entrepreneurship.about:
Launched in 2015, the Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF) Entrepreneurship Programme is the largest African philanthropic initiative for entrepreneurs, having supported thousands of businesses across all 54 African countries.

Applicants register on TEFConnect, describe their business and take a business-assessment test. Those who meet the minimum score progress to a structured online business-management training with interactive modules, followed by mentoring; the best-performing entrepreneurs receive non-refundable seed capital and join the TEF alumni network.

The application portal opens every year on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March, so the 2027 window is 1 January – 1 March 2027.

tower-poetry-competition-2027.about:

Tufts University's pre-college programmes give high-school students a taste of university study in focused one- or two-week formats, many with a health-science angle: Mini Med School, Mini Dental School, and Lab Science Investigations (for example antimicrobial-resistance research, 11–23 July 2027), plus programmes in engineering, international relations and the arts.

uclmun-xii-2026.about:
UCLMUN XII ('Creating Order out of Chaos') is the annual university conference run by UCL's United Nations Association in central London.

The conference runs 20–22 November 2026 at University College London, Gower Street, United Kingdom. It is open to university students (delegates and faculty advisors). Working language: English.

Delegate & faculty-advisor applications are open now via 'Apply Now' on the official site (chair applications have closed). The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

udga-2027.about:
The United Diplomats Global Assembly (UDGA) 2027 takes place on 25–29 January 2027 at the United Nations Conference Centre (UNCC) in Bangkok. Around 280 delegates simulate the UN General Assembly on one agenda — safe and ethical AI, AI-driven disinformation and the digital divide — and also take part in networking, a city tour and leadership sessions.

Young people can apply as individuals or as delegations. Packages range from conference-only to full experience with twin-share hotel and transfers, and a scholarship track (with a small application fee) covers 50–100% of costs.

A rare chance to debate inside a UN venue; worth considering mainly through the scholarship track because full packages are expensive.
highlights: Held at the UN Conference Centre, Bangkok
Scholarships covering 50–100% of costs
Single UNGA agenda on AI governance
